title: TikTok: One ship blocked $9.6B a day (Ever Given / Suez, map + animation)
_sources:
TikTok "One ship blocked $9.6B a day" (Ever Given, Suez 2021) -> project.json
Sources (checked 2026-10-26):
Bloomberg via Al Jazeera 25.03.2021: ~$9.6B/day of traffic held up (westbound $5.1B, eastbound $4.5B), Ever Given 400 m.
Boskalis/SMIT via gCaptain: grounded 23 Mar 2021, refloated 29 Mar 2021 15:05, ~30,000 m3 sand dredged, 11 harbour tugs + 2 seagoing tugs.
NZ MFAT "The Importance of the Suez Canal to Global Trade" (18.04.2021): ~12% of global trade, 30% of container traffic,
  ~450 vessels held up, Cape of Good Hope detour adds ~9,000 km and 6-14 days.
Empire State Building: 443 m to tip (381 m roof) -> "almost as long as ... is tall".

lines.text: This one ship blocked nine-point-six billion dollars of world trade. Every single day.
In March twenty twenty-one, the Ever Given got stuck sideways in the Suez Canal.
It's four hundred meters long. That's almost as long as the Empire State Building is tall.
And about twelve percent of all world trade goes through this one canal.
Within days, around four hundred fifty ships were stuck waiting.
The only other way is all the way around Africa. That's about nine thousand extra kilometers, and up to two weeks longer.
So diggers and dredgers removed thirty thousand cubic meters of sand, and tugboats pulled for six days.
On March twenty-ninth, the ship finally broke free!
